title: constraint search, pruning, and puzzle backtracking
concepts: Constraint search builds a partial assignment and checks whether it still satisfies constraints before investing work in deeper choices.
The most-constrained-variable heuristic chooses the variable with the fewest legal values, often exposing contradictions earlier than a fixed variable order.
Forward checking removes values made impossible by a choice; a branch with an empty remaining domain can be rejected immediately.
Symmetry breaking removes equivalent branches only when the transformation preserves the problem's solutions and does not discard a distinct required answer.
A complete solution must satisfy every constraint, while a partial solution only needs to remain extendable; local validity does not guarantee eventual completion.
Search complexity depends on branching factor and depth and may be factorial or exponential; pruning improves practical search but does not automatically improve worst-case bounds.
Bit masks can represent small domains or occupied rows, columns, and diagonals efficiently, but require careful width and shift bounds.
Backtracking correctness follows from exploring every legal choice not pruned by a sound rule and restoring all mutable state before exploring a sibling branch.

practiceProblems.name: N-Queens
practiceProblems.statement: Return every distinct placement of n queens on an n by n board such that no two queens attack each other. Each solution is represented as n strings using Q and .; output order is arbitrary.

practiceProblems.name: Sudoku Solver
patterns: choose an empty cell with few candidates
practiceProblems.statement: Fill the empty cells of a 9 by 9 Sudoku board in place so digits 1 through 9 occur exactly once in each row, column, and 3 by 3 subgrid. The input is guaranteed to have exactly one solution.
constraints: board has exactly 9 rows and 9 columns
Each cell is a digit or '.'
The puzzle has exactly one solution

practiceProblems.name: Word Search
practiceProblems.statement: Return whether a word can be formed by sequentially horizontally or vertically adjacent board cells, using no cell more than once in that path.
constraints: Board and word contain English letters of either case

practiceProblems.name: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
practiceProblems.statement: Return whether nums can be partitioned into k nonempty subsets whose sums are all equal. Every array element is used exactly once.
constraints: Each distinct value occurs between 1 and 4 times

practiceProblems.name: Matchsticks to Square
patterns: sort largest-first and prune symmetric sides
practiceProblems.statement: Use every matchstick exactly once without breaking any stick to form a square. Return whether this is possible.

practiceProblems.name: Word Search II
patterns: branch pruning against a word prefix
combine board search with trie prefix lookups
practiceProblems.statement: Return every word from the supplied unique dictionary that can be traced by horizontally or vertically adjacent board cells without reusing a cell within a word. Output order is arbitrary.

comparisons: Heuristic guess that may discard solutions
